tldr: Fitting the balancing covariate equalizes first-order precision but not the next signed risk term. Uniformly over the maintained bounded smooth iid class and every fixed public try budget, the exact moment-adjusted estimator has normalization n^2 and selector-indexed coefficient F_T^pi(P)=(v_T^pi-1)c_1(P)+(q_T^pi-3)c_2(P), where c_1=2A-B+C-D and c_2=D. This yields an attainable quadratic-score frontier over complete randomization, Wang--Li best choice, a capped Morgan--Rubin threshold rule, and score-directed selectors. Pointwise minimization of c_1 w+c_2 w^2 is exactly optimal in the class; Wang--Li best choice is strictly optimal precisely on its stated c_1<0 region, with c_1=0 the exact elbow. The result supports prospective design planning from supplied joint-outcome moments.
gap: Wang--Li Equation 19 and Theorem 8 and Li--Ding Theorem 3 establish first-order fitted precision under different rerandomization designs. They do not order the surviving signed MSE term of the same fitted moment estimator or choose an assignment selector at a common fixed try budget. Complete-randomization higher-order expansions do not resolve this design comparison.
fill: A uniform differentiated signed-CDF expansion and exact fitted-score parity must derive a common population loss. Sectional variation supplies a design-class transfer bound. An attaining selector and expected-minimum lower bound certify the optimum and the exact conditions for strict improvement over each named alternative; certified one-dimensional evaluation turns those conditions into a population-input planning rule.
